349529.title: The modulo 7 decomposition conjecture for the crank generating function
349529.statement_literal:
Let $q$ be a formal variable, and let $A$, $B$, $C$, $D$, and $E$ denote the quantities used in the paper's modulo $7$ decomposition. **The modulo 7 decomposition conjecture.**

$$
\frac{1}{(q;q)_{\infty}}\sum_{n\geq 1}\frac{(-1)^nq^{n(n+1)/2}(1-q^n)^5(1+q^n)}{1-q^{7n}}=-qA+3q^2B-2q^3C+q^4D-3q^6E.
$$

The identity is proposed as part of the decomposition used to study the paper's modulo $7$ theorem, but the supplied text does not establish the definitions of $A$, $B$, $C$, $D$, and $E$ or report a resolution.
349529.review_depth: full TeX of arXiv:2101.10910 v1 (only version): Conjecture 5.1 (lines 473-476, A..E defined at line 476), Theorem 5.2 reduction to seven equalities, six proved, (vii) open (line 693); web search for citing work (none resolving it found)
349529.disposition: No counterexample: both sides agree exactly through q^700 (A..E exactly as defined in the source). A proof needs Appell-Lerch / modular-form machinery (identity (vii) of Theorem 5.2); no finite certificate exists and Lean cost is prohibitive. The motivating Beck crank congruence mod 7 is already known (Chern). Source typo noted: the expansion line writes L N/Q for B where B = (q^49) L Q/N.

350949.title: The type A enumeration conjecture for Coxeter Pop-Tsack torsing
350949.statement_literal:
Let $A_{n-1}$ be the type $A$ Coxeter system, let $4frak S_n$ be its permutation group, and let $\mathsf{Pop}_T$ be the Coxeter Pop-Tsack map. A permutation **requires exactly $k$ iterations** of $\mathsf{Pop}_T$ to reach the identity if $k$ is the least nonnegative integer such that $\mathsf{Pop}_T^k(w)=e$. **The type A enumeration conjecture.** In type $A_{n-1}$, the number of permutations that require exactly $n-2$ or $n-1$ iterations of $\mathsf{Pop}_T$ to reach the identity is

$$
2^n-\binom{n}{2}.
$$

This refines the orbit-length analysis of the Coxeter Pop-Tsack map in type $A$ by enumerating the elements at the two greatest possible distances from the identity. The supplied text does not state whether this enumeration has been proved or remains open.
350949.review_depth: arXiv abs of source (v1 only) and of Anqi Li, Dynamics of Pop-Tsack Torsing, arXiv:2209.11548 (abstract and search-snippet level: Corollary 2.3 = [DW, Conjecture 5.5])
350949.disposition: Proved by Anqi Li (arXiv:2209.11548, 2022): Corollary 2.3 states exactly that in type A_{n-1} the number of permutations requiring n-2 or n-1 Pop_T iterations is 2^n - binom(n,2); the abstract says all enumeration conjectures of Defant-Williams are resolved.

346365.title: The vector-valued generating-function identity for standard Young tableaux and sorting networks
346365.statement_literal:
For $n\geq 2$, let $\operatorname{SYT}(\delta_n)$ be the set of standard Young tableaux of staircase shape $\delta_n$, let $\operatorname{SN}_n$ be the set of sorting networks on $n$ elements, and let $f_t(x_1,\ldots,x_{n-1})$ and $g_s(x_1,\ldots,x_{n-1})$ be the associated generating-function coefficients, with basis vectors $\sigma_t$ and $\pi_s$. **The generating-function identity.** For $n\geq 2$,

$$
\sum_{t\in \operatorname{SYT}(\delta_n)} f_t(x_1,\ldots,x_{n-1})\sigma_t = \sum_{s\in \operatorname{SN}_n} g_s(x_1,\ldots,x_{n-1})\pi_s.
$$

This is presented as an algebraic-combinatorial reformulation of the conjectural equality in distribution between the oriented swap process and last passage percolation vectors. Its status is not resolved by the supplied text.
346365.review_depth: full TeX of arXiv:2005.02043 (Conjecture main-conj-reformulated; Section "Equivalence of combinatorial and probabilistic conjectures", line 1093); arXiv abs of L. Zhang arXiv:2107.06350 v3 (Adv. Math.)
346365.disposition: The generating-function identity F_n = G_n is proved in the source to be equivalent to the OSP/LPP distributional conjecture, which Lingfu Zhang proved (arXiv:2107.06350, shift-invariance of colored TASEP); Zhang's abstract states the equivalence with the combinatorial Edelman-Greene identity.

347198.title: Combinatorial identity equivalent to the hypergeometric contribution conjecture
347198.statement_literal:
Fix an integer $d\geq 1$. Let $(d_1,\ldots,d_r)\vdash d$ range over strictly positive unordered partitions of $d$, and let $\#\operatorname{Aut}(d_1,\ldots,d_r)$ denote the order of the automorphism group of the partition.

**Combinatorial identity conjecture.** Then

$$
\sum_{(d_1,\ldots,d_r)\vdash d}\dfrac{2^{r-1}\cdot d^{r-2}}{\#\operatorname{Aut}(d_1,\ldots,d_r)}\prod_{i=1}^r\dfrac{(-1)^{d_i-1}}{d_i}{3d_i\choose d_i}=\dfrac{1}{d^2}{4d-1\choose d}.
$$

The paper presents this identity as a purely combinatorial formula equivalent to the first hypergeometric contribution formula, providing theoretical evidence for that conjecture. The supplied text gives no independent resolution of this identity.
347198.review_depth: full TeX of arXiv:2007.05016 v3 (Crelle): Conjecture conj:combinatorial conjecture (line 2151), Proposition 6.13 equivalence, Remark (Reineke / 3-Kronecker quiver, line 2145)
347198.disposition: True for all d by a five-line classical argument: sum over partitions with 1/Aut = (1/r!) times ordered compositions, so LHS = [x^d] exp(2d A(x)) / (2 d^2), A(x) = sum (-1)^(m-1) binom(3m,m)/m x^m = -3 log B(-x) with B = 1 + x B^3 (Lagrange inversion); then exp(2dA) = B(-x)^(-6d) and [x^d] B^r = r/(3d+r) binom(3d+r,d) at r = -6d gives 2 binom(4d-1,d). Exact check d <= 30 (direct sum and series route agree). Zero credit: a routine Lagrange-inversion bridge (the source itself remarks the formula is the Reineke-proved Kronecker-quiver coefficient after taking logarithms).

341837.title: Gregory–Newton summation identity for signed pancake distances
341837.statement_literal:
Let $R_k^B(n)$ denote the number of signed permutations of size $n$ whose burnt-pancake distance from the sorted stack is $k$. **Summation identity conjecture.** If $k,n\geq1$, then

$$
R_k^B(n)=\sum_{j=1}^k\left(\sum_{i=0}^{k-j}(-1)^i\binom{i+j-1}{i}\binom{n}{i+j}\right)R_k^B(j).
$$

The identity is observed in the source and is motivated by the assertion that the functions $R_k^B(n)$ are integer-valued polynomials together with the Gregory–Newton interpolation formula. No proof or resolution is supplied, so it remains open.
341837.review_depth: full TeX of arXiv:1902.04055 v4 (DMTCS version): Table tab:bn, Conjecture con:bn, Conjecture con:sum (Concluding Remarks, incl. commented-out text); full TeX of Blanco-Skora arXiv:2302.03929 v2 (ISSAC 2023) Section 4 (lines 390-488); Labarre-Cibulka arXiv:1010.0219 TeX (no reduction lemma)
341837.disposition: As printed (coefficient binom(i+j-1,i)) the identity is FALSE: e.g. k = n = 3 gives 14 but R_3^B(3) = 12 (source's own table); 21 failing cells for n <= 7. This is a misprint (zero-credit source-internal correction); with binom(i+j,i) it is ordinary Gregory-Newton interpolation and holds in every cell (exact BFS of all signed permutations, n <= 7, reproduces the source table). The intended statement is KNOWN: Blanco-Skora (arXiv:2302.03929, ISSAC 2023) prove burnt-pancake distance classes are grid signed permutation classes enumerated by polynomials for all n and state that [BBP19, Conjecture 6.3] follows by Gregory-Newton. Independent short proof found here (zero credit): deleting a pancake commutes with flips (distance non-increasing), and an adjacency strip acts as one burnt pancake, so distance is invariant under strip reduction; hence R_k^B(n) = sum_{b<=k} binom(n,b) I_k(b), I_k(b) = # adjacency-free signed perms of size b at distance k (verified n <= 7, 0 violations).

339353.title: Byszewski–Ulas digit-sum summation conjecture for powers of binary sums
339353.statement_literal:
Let $r\ge 1$, let $N_1,\ldots,N_r$ be positive integers, and let $x,y_1,\ldots,y_r$ be variables. For each nonnegative integer $n$, write $s_2(n)$ for the sum of the binary digits of $n$. **Byszewski–Ulas conjecture.** One has

$$
\sum_{n_1=0}^{2^{N_1}-1}\cdots\sum_{n_r=0}^{2^{N_r}-1}(-1)^{\sum_{j=1}^r s_2(n_j)}\left(x+\sum_{j=1}^r n_j y_j\right)^{\sum_{j=1}^r N_j}=(-1)^{\sum_{j=1}^r N_r}2^{\sum_{j=1}^r\frac{N_j(N_j-1)}{2}}\left(\prod_{j=1}^r y_j^{N_j}\right)\left(\sum_{j=1}^r N_j\right)!.
$$

The paper states that this conjecture is proved and generalized there; the displayed identity concerns weighted power sums arising from the binary digit-sum function.
339353.review_depth: full TeX of arXiv:1805.10569 v1 (only version): Conjecture conj42 (lines 80-85) and Proposition in Section "Conjecture 1" (lines 355-366)
339353.disposition: This is Byszewski-Ulas Conjecture 4.2; Wakhare-Vignat prove it (and its base-b generalization) in the source itself.

339354.title: Byszewski–Ulas digit-sum factorization conjecture
339354.statement_literal:
Let $r\ge 1$, let $N_1,\ldots,N_r$ be positive integers, and let $x_1,\ldots,x_r,y_1,\ldots,y_r$ be variables. For each nonnegative integer $n$, write $s_2(n)$ for the sum of the binary digits of $n$. **Byszewski–Ulas conjecture.** One has

$$
\sum_{n_1=0}^{2^{N_1}-1}\cdots\sum_{n_r=0}^{2^{N_r}-1}(-1)^{\sum_{j=1}^r s_2(n_j)}\left(\sum_{j=1}^r s_2(n_j)x_j+n_jy_j\right)^{\sum_{j=1}^r N_j}=(-1)^{\sum_{j=1}^r N_r}\left(\sum_{j=1}^r N_j\right)!\prod_{j=1}^r\prod_{i_j=0}^{N_j-1}(x_j+2^{i_j}y_j).
$$

The paper presents this as another conjecture of Byszewski and Ulas and states in the introduction that it proves and generalizes the two displayed conjectures. The identity gives a product factorization for a digit-sum-weighted power sum.
339354.review_depth: full TeX of arXiv:1805.10569 v1: Conjecture conj44 (lines 86-91), Theorem thm12 (line 450 ff.)
339354.disposition: Byszewski-Ulas Conjecture 4.4; proved (with base-b generalization) as Theorem thm12 of the source.

339772.title: The refined pipe-dream and quarter-plane walk bijection conjecture
339772.statement_literal: Fix integers $n$ and $k$. Consider pipe dreams $P$ with $\omega_P\in\mathfrak{S}_n$ whose factorization into atomics consists of $k$ identity permutations, and quarter-plane walks starting at $(0,0)$, ending on the horizontal axis, consisting of $2n$ steps from $\{(-1,1),(1,-1),(0,1)\}$, with exactly $k$ steps equal to $(0,1)$. **Refined pipe-dream and walk conjecture.** These two families have the same cardinality. This is a stronger refinement of the preceding dimension conjecture and is stated as a conjectural bijective correspondence between the two families.
339772.review_depth: full TeX of arXiv:1807.03044 v4 (JLMS 2022): Conjectures conj:walks1, conj:walks2, Lemmas bouncepairs/coloredDyckpaths, Conjecture conj:SteepBounce with footnote (lines 1222-1340)
339772.disposition: The source shows conj:walks2 is equivalent (via its Lemmas on bounce pairs and colored Dyck paths) to the Steep-Bounce Conjecture, and the v4 footnote states that conjecture "has been solved in [CeballosFangMuhle]" (Ceballos-Fang-Muhle, steep-bounce zeta map).

340504.title: Kanade--Russell Conjecture I_1 on partition identities
340504.statement_literal:
For a nonnegative integer $n$, consider partitions into parts congruent to $1$, $3$, $6$, or $8$ modulo $9$. Also consider partitions satisfying the **difference at least $3$ at distance $2$** condition, meaning that each part exceeds the part two positions later by at least $3$, and such that whenever two consecutive parts differ by at most $1$, their sum is divisible by $3$. **Kanade--Russell Conjecture $I_1$.** The number of partitions of $n$ into parts congruent to $1$, $3$, $6$, or $8$ modulo $9$ equals the number of partitions of $n$ satisfying the stated difference and consecutive-part conditions.

This is one of six Rogers--Ramanujan-type partition-identity conjectures proposed by Kanade and Russell. The source presents it as a conjecture and gives no resolution.
340504.review_depth: arXiv abs of source (Chern-Li v3), of Rosengren arXiv:1912.03689, of Xia arXiv:2609.08816; GitHub repository yuma-mizuno/KR-mod9-lean README (API receipt)
340504.disposition: The mod 9 Kanade-Russell identities are proved: Xia (arXiv:2609.08816, Sep 2026) proves all five mod 9 sum-product identities, and Y. Mizuno (arXiv:2609.09653) with a public kernel-checked Lean 4 formalization (github.com/yuma-mizuno/KR-mod9-lean, created 2026-09-09) of the three mod 9 sum = product identities, including 1/(q,q^3,q^6,q^8;q^9). With the known sum-side/partition correspondence (Kurşungöz; Chern-Li) this settles I_1. Excluded (public Lean prior art).

336313.title: The permutation-equivariance conjecture for the rigged-configuration bijection
336313.statement_literal:
Let $B = \bigotimes_{k=1}^N B^{r_k,s_k}$ and let $B' = \bigotimes_{k=1}^N B^{r'_k,s'_k}$ be any reordering of the same tensor factors. Let $\operatorname{RC}(B)$ and $\operatorname{RC}(B')$ be the corresponding rigged-configuration models, let $\Phi$ be the crystal bijection, and let $R\colon B\to B'$ be the crystal isomorphism induced by the reordering.

**Permutation-equivariance conjecture.** The diagram relating $\operatorname{RC}(B)$ to $\operatorname{RC}(B')$ by the identity and $B$ to $B'$ by $R$, with vertical maps given by $\Phi$, commutes for any reordering $B'$.

This asserts that the rigged-configuration bijection is compatible with reordering tensor factors. It is stated conjecturally in the supplied source, with no resolution indicated.
336313.review_depth: full TeX of arXiv:1706.02443 v3 (AHP 2019): Conjectures conj:bijection and conj:R_matrix_identity (lines 1403-1425) and the status paragraph
336313.disposition: Recalled conjecture (Schilling-Scrimshaw et al.): known for nonexceptional types (KSS02, OSSS16, OSS17) and many special exceptional cases; the remaining cases need the general (box-splitting) RC bijection in exceptional types, which the source does not even define. No finite certificate model; implementing KR crystals and Phi from scratch is out of scope.

336450.title: Binomial-transform conjecture for classical and enhanced k-crossing-avoiding partitions
336450.statement_literal:
For $k\geq2$, let $C_k(n)$ be the number of partitions of $[n]$ avoiding classical $k$-crossings, and let $E_k(n)$ be the number avoiding enhanced $k$-crossings. **Binomial-transform conjecture.** Fix $k\geq2$. The following identity holds:

$$
C_k(n+1)=\sum_{i=0}^n{n\choose i}E_k(i).
$$

The identity extends the known Catalan–Motzkin relation for $k=2$ and the corresponding identity for $k=3$. A proof is suggested as an open direction via bijections for crossing-avoiding partitions, and the source gives no resolution.
336450.review_depth: arXiv abs of source (Lin, EJC 2018) and of Gil-Tirrell arXiv:1806.09065 v2 (Discrete Math. 343 (2020) 111705)
336450.disposition: Proved by Gil and Tirrell (arXiv:1806.09065, Discrete Math. 2020): their extension map gives a combinatorial proof of the binomial-transform relation, explicitly resolving Lin's conjecture; Lin-Kim (arXiv:1905.10526) give a refinement.

333320.title: The retract characterization conjecture for hypercellular graphs
333320.statement_literal:
Let $G$ be a partial cube. A **retract** of a graph $H$ is a subgraph admitting a graph homomorphism from $H$ to the subgraph that restricts to the identity on the subgraph. A Cartesian product of graphs is formed by taking vertex tuples and joining tuples that differ in exactly one coordinate along an edge in that factor. Bipartite cellular graphs are the class used in the paper.

**The retract characterization conjecture.** A partial cube $G$ is hypercellular if and only if $G$ is a retract of a Cartesian product of bipartite cellular graphs.

This is proposed as an analogue of the fact that median graphs are precisely retracts of hypercubes. The supplied text gives no resolution, so the conjecture remains open.
333320.review_depth: full TeX of arXiv:1606.02154 v3 (Discrete Math. 2020): Conjecture retract (line 2056, "(weak) retract"), the C6-plus-pendant-edge remark, commented-out draft proposition (line 1650); web search for follow-ups (none found)
333320.disposition: Open structural conjecture (source says "(weak) retract"; one direction follows from the source's closure of hypercellular graphs under products and retracts). A refutation would require excluding retractions into every product of bipartite cellular graphs (no finite certificate); a proof needs a new retraction construction. Lean cost (partial cubes, Theta-classes, gated amalgams) very high. Parked.

328917.title: A generalized Prouhet–Thue–Morse identity for products of binary sums
328917.statement_literal:
Let $k\geq 1$ and let $a_{1},\ldots,a_{k}$ be nonnegative integers. Put $A=(a_{1},\ldots,a_{k})$ and let $X=(x,x_{1},\ldots,x_{k})$ be a vector of variables. Define

$$
G_{A}(X)=\sum_{i_{1}=0}^{2^{a_{1}}-1}\cdots\sum_{i_{k}=0}^{2^{a_{k}}-1}(-1)^{\sum_{j=1}^{k}s_{2}(i_{j})}\Bigl(x+\sum_{j=1}^{k}i_{j}x_{j}\Bigr)^{\sum_{j=1}^{k}a_{j}}.
$$

**The generalized Prouhet–Thue–Morse identity.** One has

$$
G_{A}(X)=(-1)^{\sum_{j=1}^{k}a_{j}}2^{\sum_{j=1}^{k}\frac{a_{j}(a_{j}-1)}{2}}\Bigl(\sum_{j=1}^{k}a_{j}\Bigr)!\prod_{j=1}^{k}x_{j}^{a_{j}}.
$$

This is proposed as a generalization of identities proved earlier in the paper for the Prouhet–Thue–Morse sequence. Its status is not established in the supplied text.
328917.review_depth: full TeX of arXiv:1409.8118 v1 (Section 4 conjectures, line 609) and of Wakhare-Vignat arXiv:1805.10569
328917.disposition: The displayed identity is Byszewski-Ulas Conjecture 4.2 (same identity as 339353 with renamed variables), proved by Wakhare-Vignat (arXiv:1805.10569) in arbitrary base. Also in the credited 342364 Ulas family neighbourhood.

329388.title: Tucker's conjecture for closed subdegree-finite permutation groups
329388.statement_literal: Let $Gamma$ be a closed, subdegree finite permutation group acting on a set $S$. A **distinguishing $2$-colouring** of $S$ is a colouring with two colours that is preserved by no non-identity element of $Gamma$. **Tucker's permutation-group conjecture.** There is a distinguishing $2$-colouring of $S$. This is presented as a generalisation of Tucker's graph-theoretic conjecture. The paper discusses related positive results, but the statement itself is not resolved there.
329388.review_depth: arXiv abs of Lehner-Moller arXiv:1412.0881 v2; TeX skimmed
329388.disposition: Tucker's conjecture (permutation-group form for closed subdegree-finite groups): famous open infinite statement (graph version still open beyond partial growth results); no finite certificate route.

324921.title: Characteristic-two dimension conjecture for 2-spec matrix spaces
324921.statement_literal:
Let $\mathbb{K}$ be a field of characteristic $2$ with more than $2$ elements, and let $\mathcal{V}$ be a $2$-spec subspace of $\operatorname{M}_n(\mathbb{K})$. **Characteristic-two 2-spec dimension conjecture.** If $n=3$ or $n\geq 5$, then

$$
\dim \mathcal{V}\leq \binom{n}{2}+3.
$$

If $n=4$, then

$$
\dim \mathcal{V}\leq \binom{n}{2}+4.
$$

The characteristic-not-$2$ analogue with bound $\binom{n}{2}+2$ is proved earlier in the paper, while examples show that characteristic $2$ requires the larger bounds above; the two-element field is excluded because every linear subspace is a $2$-spec space.
324921.review_depth: arXiv abs of source; full TeX of de Seguins Pazzis, Spaces of matrices with few eigenvalues (II), arXiv:2605.05849 v1 (May 2026): Theorem theorem:maintheodim2spec
324921.disposition: Proved: arXiv:2605.05849 Theorem maintheodim2spec: for char F = 2, |F| > 2, n >= 3, the greatest dimension of a 2-spec subspace of M_n(F) is binom(n,2)+3 if n != 4 and binom(n,2)+4 if n = 4 (bounds attained, e.g. sl_2 v sl_2 for n = 4).

323534.title: Truncated Jacobi identity for the three-colour partition function
323534.statement_literal:
Let $t(n)$ be defined by

$$
\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}t(n)q^n=\frac{1}{(q)_\infty^3}.
$$

Thus $t(n)$ counts partitions of $n$ into three kinds of parts. **Truncated Jacobi conjecture.** For $n,k\geqslant 1$, there holds

$$
(-1)^k\sum_{j=0}^k(-1)^j(2j+1)t\bigl(n-j(j+1)/2\bigr)\geqslant 0,
$$

with strict inequality if $n\geqslant (k+1)(k+2)/2$.

This is a sign conjecture for the partial sums arising from Jacobi's identity for $(q)_\infty^3$. The paper gives initial examples but does not provide a proof or resolution.
323534.review_depth: full TeX of arXiv:1205.4340 v2 (final conjecture, t(n)); He-Ji-Zang, Bilateral truncated Jacobi's identity (Eur. J. Combin. 2016) PDF (abstract, Section 1 incl. Corollary 1.2 and its special case (1.7))
323534.disposition: Proved: Mao (2015, algebraic) and He-Ji-Zang (EJC 2016, combinatorial; their Corollary 1.2, with the strict inequality, contains Guo-Zeng's conjecture (1.7) as a special case).

323795.title: Fischer–Riegler conjecture for vertically symmetric alternating-sign matrices
323795.statement_literal:
Let $\alpha(n;k_1,\ldots,k_n)$ denote the generalized monotone-triangle enumeration, and let $n\geq1$. An alternating-sign matrix (ASM) is a square matrix with entries in $\{-1,0,1\}$ whose row and column sums are $1$, with nonzero entries alternating in every row and column. **Fischer–Riegler conjecture.** The identity

$$
\alpha(2n+1;2n+1,2n,\ldots,1)=(-1)^n\alpha(n;2,4,\ldots,2n)
$$

should hold; moreover, $\alpha(n;2,4,\ldots,2n)$ counts vertically symmetric ASMs of size $2n+1$. This is one of several identities conjectured from computational evidence, and the source highlights the interest of finding bijective proofs.
323795.review_depth: full TeX of arXiv:1207.4437 v1 (only version; DMTCS FPSAC 2013 version not separately read): conjectures section (lines 1205-1300); web search (no proof found)
323795.disposition: No counterexample: alpha(2n+1;2n+1,...,1) = (-1)^n alpha(n;2,...,2n) verified exactly for n <= 6 (argument length 13) with an exact evaluator of alpha at arbitrary integer points (Fischer's generalized-summation recursion; validated on ASM numbers, VSASM numbers and the proved combinatorial-reciprocity identity). n = 7 exceeds the 2 GB lane cap. A proof would be a new ASM-type identity; Lean cost of the alpha operator formula is very high. Parked.

323796.title: Even-argument reciprocity conjecture for generalized monotone triangles
323796.statement_literal:
Let $\alpha(n;k_1,\ldots,k_n)$ denote the generalized monotone-triangle enumeration, and let $n\geq1$. **Even-argument reciprocity conjecture.** The identity

$$
\alpha(n;2,4,\ldots,2n)=\alpha(2n;2n,2n,2n-2,2n-2,\ldots,2,2)
$$

should hold. The paper lists this among identities supported by mathematical computation and explains that the combinatorial interpretation supplied by generalized monotone triangles makes bijective proofs desirable; no proof is supplied here.
323796.review_depth: full TeX of arXiv:1207.4437 v1 conjectures section
323796.disposition: No counterexample: alpha(n;2,4,...,2n) = alpha(2n;2n,2n,...,2,2) verified exactly for n <= 6 (values 1, 3, 26, 646, 45885, 9304650). Same evaluator and limits as 323795. Parked.

323799.title: Reverse-duplication conjecture for generalized monotone triangles
323799.statement_literal:
Let $A_n:=\alpha(n;1,2,\ldots,n)$, and let $n\geq1$, $i=1,\ldots,n-k+1$, and $k=1,\ldots,n$. **Reverse-duplication conjecture.** The identity

$$
A_n=\alpha(n+k;1,\ldots,i-1,i+k-1,i+k-1,i+k-2,i+k-2,\ldots,i,i,i+k,i+k+1,\ldots,n)
$$

should hold. In words, the consecutive subsequence $(i,i+1,\ldots,i+k-1)$ is reversed, each entry is duplicated, and the resulting block is inserted back into $(1,2,\ldots,n)$. The paper notes that the previously stated identity is the case $k=2$, while the earlier combinatorial-reciprocity identity is the case $k=n$; the general statement remains computationally conjectural.
323799.review_depth: full TeX of arXiv:1207.4437 v1 conjectures section (Conjecture revDupConj)
323799.disposition: No counterexample: the reverse-duplication identity verified exactly for every k = 1..n and i = 1..n-k+1 for all n <= 7 (28 cases at n = 7, A_7 = 218348); n = 8 exceeds the 2 GB cap. Parked.

372772.title: Filliman's extremal projection conjecture for the regular simplex
372772.statement_literal:
Let $\Delta_n$ be the regular $n$-simplex in $\mathbb{R}^n$. Fix $1\leq k\leq n$, and let $H_{\ast}$ be a $k$-dimensional subspace such that $T_{\ast}=\operatorname{Proj}_{H_{\ast}}(\Delta_n)$ is a $k$-dimensional simplex. Suppose the vertices of $\Delta_n$ project only onto the vertices of $T_{\ast}$, as evenly as possible: if $w_i$ is the number projecting onto vertex $i$ of $T_{\ast}$, then, writing $n+1=(k+1)\ell+r$ with $r\in\{0,\ldots,k\}$, one has

$$
w_i=\begin{cases}\ell+1,&1\leq i\leq r,\\ell,&r<i\leq k+1.
\end{cases}
$$

**Filliman's conjecture.** The minimum $k$-dimensional projection volume is attained by $T_{\ast}$:

$$
\min_{\substack{H\subset\mathbb{R}^n\\dim H=k}}\operatorname{vol}_k(\operatorname{Proj}_H(\Delta_n))=\operatorname{vol}_k(T_{\ast}).
$$

Moreover, for $T^{\ast}=\operatorname{Proj}_{H_{\ast}^{\perp}}(\Delta_n)$, the maximum $(n-k)$-dimensional projection volume is attained by $T^{\ast}$:

$$
\max_{\substack{H\subset\mathbb{R}^n\\dim H=n-k}}\operatorname{vol}_{n-k}(\operatorname{Proj}_H(\Delta_n))=\operatorname{vol}_{n-k}(T^{\ast}).
$$

The conjecture proposes the extremal volumes for projections of the regular simplex onto complementary-dimensional subspaces; the stated source does not provide evidence resolving it, so its status remains open.
372772.review_depth: full TeX of arXiv:2601.18436 v1: Conjecture conj:Filliman and status paragraph (lines 141-156)
372772.disposition: Filliman's conjecture dates from 1990 (not 2026, as the metadata says); proved by Filliman for k = 1, 2, n-1 and n <= 6 (minimum), with further partial cases for the maximum. Continuous extremal problem over Grassmannians, no finite certificate; analytic and deep. Parked.
